cases.title: Shaanxi Ankang Road Development: 698 households moved for the Ankang-Maoba expressway
cases.place: Ankang-Maoba expressway and local roads, Ankang, Shaanxi, China
cases.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on the city of Ankang in southern Shaanxi. The loan paid for an 87 km expressway running from Ankang south to Maoba, near the Sichuan border, and for local road works in Ziyang County, Hanbin District and Langao County. Land was taken along the whole corridor, not at this point.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Shaanxi Ankang Road Development Project, P075613. Loan IBRD-48530 (IBRD 4853-CHA) of US$300 million, approved 13 March 2007, effective 10 August 2007. The closing date moved from 30 June 2012 to 31 December 2012. The loan was fully disbursed at US$300 million. The project was Environmental Category A.

cases.conditions: The loan triggered the Bank's policy on involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12). Resettlement Plans and a Resettlement Policy Framework were prepared before approval. The completion report says compensation rates were set to reflect Chinese regulations and the restoration demands of the affected people, and that about 120 meetings were held with affected and local people on resettlement policy, compensation, restoration and grievances.

companies.name: Ankang Municipal Communications Bureau
companies.role: Implementing agency for the local road improvement programme

cases.community: The completion report records what the project took. It acquired 5,713 mu of land permanently, about 381 hectares, of which 3,040 mu, about 203 hectares, was farmland. It took a further 2,459 mu, about 164 hectares, temporarily. It relocated 698 households with 2,998 persons and affected 11 enterprises. RMB 262 million was spent on carrying out the resettlement. The Independent Evaluation Group's review gives the same land in metric units: 3.8 million square metres taken permanently and 1.63 million square metres temporarily. The report says all the affected people were identified, consulted, compensated and resettled, and that the external resettlement monitor's survey and evaluation concluded that the affected households restored their income and their housing condition. No named village or neighbourhood appears in either document.
cases.outcome: The resettlement is recorded as compliant. The completion report of 13 June 2013 rates safeguard and fiduciary compliance Satisfactory and says the social safeguard implementation was satisfactory and strictly followed the resettlement plans and the framework. The completion report rates the project outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory, borrower performance Satisfactory and risk to the development outcome Low or Negligible. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 22 September 2014 also rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, but rates Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory, borrower performance Moderately Satisfactory and risk to the development outcome Moderate. The Evaluation Group gives its reason for the lower borrower rating as the Ankang municipal government not providing counterpart funds in a timely manner, which delayed the local roads component, and for the lower Bank rating that insufficient road safety measures were prepared and inappropriate outcome indicators were selected. Neither document records a failure in the resettlement.
cases.displaced_label: persons relocated, in 698 households (World Bank completion report)
cases.displaced_note: The World Bank's completion report gives the outcome: 698 households with 2,998 persons relocated, 11 enterprises affected, 5,713 mu of land taken permanently including 3,040 mu of farmland, and 2,459 mu taken temporarily. ICIJ puts displacement for this project at 171,568 and lists it as confirmed displacement. On ICIJ's own account of its method, its figures count what the Bank's documents call project-affected people: ICIJ searched those documents for the words "affected", "PAP" and "displaced", used the average household size where a document counted only households, and, because the documents do not consistently separate temporary impacts from permanent ones, "decided to include all impacts", down to a loss as small as under one per cent of a person's land or income. It drew mainly on resettlement action plans, which are written before the work is done, and used completion reports where no resettlement plan existed. Its data stops at 31 December 2014. No figure matching 171,568 appears in the completion report or in the Independent Evaluation Group's review, and the documents do not say how ICIJ arrived at it.

cases.place: Secondary tributaries of the Huai River in Anhui, Jiangsu, Henan and Shandong, China
cases.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on Bengbu, on the main stem of the Huai River in Anhui. The project worked on smaller tributaries spread across four provinces, Anhui, Jiangsu, Henan and Shandong, in a basin the completion report gives as 270,000 square kilometres, so no single point covers it.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Huai River Basin Flood Management and Drainage Improvement Project, P098078. Loan IBRD-79380 (Loan 7938-CN) of US$200 million, approved 6 July 2010, effective 26 January 2011, restructured 15 June 2016, closed 31 December 2016. The loan was fully disbursed at US$200 million.

cases.conditions: The loan triggered the Bank's policy on involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12), its policy on physical cultural resources (OP 4.11) and its policy on natural habitats (OP 4.04). The completion report says a full resettlement action plan was prepared and carried out for each subproject, that social provisions were written into every construction contract, that resettlement offices were set up, and that the project management offices engaged both internal and external monitors to track the plans.

companies.name: Huai River Water Resources Commission

cases.community: The completion report records that changes to the engineering designs cut the number of people needing resettlement from 7,044 to 4,884 across the four provinces. It says a survey showed that the incomes and living conditions of all resettled people were at least maintained, and that the project fully complied with the Bank's resettlement policy. The documents do not name a village or a township where people moved, and they do not separate people who lost housing from people who lost only land or income. During the works 10 cultural sites were found in Jiangsu province; the completion report says the site has been preserved.
cases.outcome: The resettlement is recorded as compliant. The completion report of 20 June 2017 rates the project outcome Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory, borrower performance Satisfactory and risk to the development outcome Moderate. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 7 September 2017 agrees on every one of those ratings and records no disagreement with the completion report. Neither document records a failure in the resettlement. The project also had a benefit target, to improve the incomes of 57,173 project-affected people, which the completion report reports as exceeded at 81,311 people; that is a count of people the project was meant to help, not a count of people moved.

It drew mainly on resettlement action plans, which are written before the work is done, and used completion reports where no resettlement plan existed. Its data stops at 31 December 2014. No figure matching 58,659 appears in the completion report or in the Independent Evaluation Group's review, and the documents do not say how ICIJ arrived at it. The project had a separate benefit target, to improve the incomes of 57,173 project-affected people, reported as exceeded at 81,311; that is a count of people the works were meant to help, not a count of people moved.

cases.title: Liaoning Medium Cities: a plan for 31,547 people, 6,080 moved
cases.place: Liaoyang, Panjin, Jinzhou, Fushun and Benxi municipalities and the county town of Dengta, Liaoning, China
cases.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on the city of Liaoyang. The project ran in six places: the municipalities of Panjin, Jinzhou, Fushun, Benxi and Liaoyang, and the county town of Dengta within Liaoyang municipality. Resettlement was scattered across all six.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Liaoning Medium Cities Infrastructure Project, P099992. Loan IBRD-48310 of US$218 million, approved 27 June 2006, signed 18 October 2006, effective 5 January 2007, restructured 18 September 2011. The closing date moved from 31 December 2011 to 31 October 2013. US$212.82 million of the US$218 million was disbursed. The road component was budgeted at US$330.93 million including US$105.1 million of resettlement costs.

cases.conditions: The loan triggered the Bank's policy on involuntary resettlement. A resettlement plan was prepared before approval, covering 4,994 households, 677 enterprises and shops and 31,547 people in the six project cities. The completion report says the local governments carried out the land acquisition and resettlement, that an independent consulting firm monitored the whole process through consultation meetings, document reviews and interviews with affected people, and that Bank supervision missions looked at compensation levels for people with and without land titles as set in the plan.

companies.name: Liaoning Urban Construction Project Office (LUCPRO)
companies.role: Provincial project office coordinating the six cities

cases.community: The figures in the completion report show the plan and the outcome side by side. The original resettlement plan covered 4,994 households, 677 enterprises and shops and 31,547 people. The report states that actual resettlement was scaled down because project components were cancelled or adjusted, and that the final resettlement involved 2,467 households, 119 enterprises and shops and 6,080 people. Most of the resettlement was finished in all six project cities before the loan closed. The first external monitoring report reached the Bank in March 2007, and separate post-evaluations of the resettlement were carried out in the project cities in 2010 and 2011. The report says the resettlement was consistently rated satisfactory during supervision and at completion, for its consultation and participatory process and its compliance with the plans. No single village or neighbourhood is named. Slow resettlement is listed in the report, alongside shortages of counterpart funds and policy changes, as one reason implementation ran slowly in 2008 and 2009.
cases.outcome: The resettlement is recorded as compliant. The completion report of 29 April 2014 rates the project outcome Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory, borrower performance Moderately Satisfactory and risk to the development outcome Low. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 5 December 2014 gives the same four ratings and records no disagreement. Separately, the external audit report for 2007 identified what the completion report calls serious issues of non-compliance in the use of Bank funds in the Panjin and Fushun jurisdictions, which held 21 per cent and 13 per cent of the loan. In Panjin, RMB 19.89 million had been claimed for work that did not conform to stated specifications. In Fushun, RMB 7.7 million had been claimed for work the Bank had not approved, and the quality of some other work did not conform to specifications. Financial management implementation was rated Unsatisfactory in the April 2009 implementation report; Fushun agreed to return the RMB 7.7 million and took action against the officials responsible. That finding concerned the use of loan funds, not the resettlement.
cases.displaced_label: people in the final resettlement, in 2,467 households, against 31,547 people in the original plan (World Bank completion report)
cases.displaced_note: The World Bank's completion report gives both the plan and the outcome. The original resettlement plan covered 4,994 households, 677 enterprises and shops and 31,547 people in six cities. The final resettlement involved 2,467 households, 119 enterprises and shops and 6,080 people, the report stating that actual resettlement was scaled down because project components were cancelled or adjusted. ICIJ puts displacement for this project at 31,547 and lists it as confirmed displacement. That is, to the person, the people figure in the original resettlement plan. On ICIJ's own account of its method, its figures count what the Bank's documents call project-affected people: ICIJ searched those documents for the words "affected", "PAP" and "displaced", used the average household size where a document counted only households, and, because the documents do not consistently separate temporary impacts from permanent ones, "decided to include all impacts", down to a loss as small as under one per cent of a person's land or income. It drew mainly on resettlement action plans, which are written before the work is done, and used completion reports where no resettlement plan existed. Its data stops at 31 December 2014. Of the projects in this group, this is the one where the plan figure and the recorded outcome are set out most plainly side by side in the lender's own report: 31,547 planned, 6,080 recorded.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: NanGuang Railway Project, P112359. Loan IBRD-77220 of US$300 million, approved 24 June 2009, effective 21 December 2009, restructured 25 August 2011 and 14 October 2014. The closing date moved from 31 December 2014 to 30 June 2015. US$297.54 million of the US$300 million was disbursed. The project was Environmental Category A.

cases.conditions: The loan triggered the Bank's policy on involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12), its policy on natural habitats and its policy on physical cultural resources. A resettlement action plan was written and published before approval, based on an inventory of physical impacts, a census of the affected population and public consultations with affected villages and households from early 2008 on the choice of railway alignment, the siting of stations, compensation rates, relocation arrangements and livelihood restoration. The plan was disclosed through a government website, local newspapers and Bank offices.

companies.name: Nanning-Guangzhou Railway Company Limited
companies.role: Special purpose company incorporated in July 2009 to build and run the line; it carried out the land acquisition and relocation

companies.name: Ministry of Railways, Foreign Capital and Technical Import Center
companies.role: Borrower's agency; it recruited the external resettlement monitoring team

cases.community: Three World Bank documents cover this resettlement, one of them a field assessment. The completion report records that at closure the implementing agency had acquired 16 square kilometres of land against 17 square kilometres estimated at appraisal, and had relocated 2,463 households against 2,029 estimated at appraisal, and that the total compensation paid for land acquisition and relocation was equivalent to the amount estimated at appraisal. In 2018 the Independent Evaluation Group sent a mission that interviewed the project's resettlement specialist. Its assessment report records that the purchase of the right of way affected farmers to a varying extent, that the overall impact in a typical village was small, that those affected were compensated through a mix of cash payments and the re-allocation of land among farmers within a village, that affected households were relocated within their own villages, and that each affected household signed a formal agreement with the local government for its relocation. The external monitoring team, recruited from a list of candidates the Bank recommended, concluded that the resettlement plan was implemented satisfactorily. The Bank's safeguards team supervised the plan once or twice a year. More households moved than the appraisal estimated, 2,463 against 2,029; that is a fact about the estimate, and neither document records anyone being harmed by the overrun. No individual village is named in any of the three documents.
cases.outcome: The resettlement is recorded as compliant by three separate documents. The completion report of 3 December 2015 rates the project outcome Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory, borrower performance Satisfactory and risk to the development outcome Negligible. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 9 June 2016 gives the same four ratings with no disagreement. The Evaluation Group's Project Performance Assessment Report of 26 June 2018, which is based on a field mission, again gives the same four ratings. The 2018 report concludes that the Bank's supervision found the implementing entities and local governments showed strong capacity on social safeguards. None of the three records a failure in the resettlement.

None of the three Bank documents gives a number of people, only households. ICIJ puts displacement for this project at 25,784 and lists it as confirmed displacement. On ICIJ's own account of its method, its figures count what the Bank's documents call project-affected people: ICIJ searched those documents for the words "affected", "PAP" and "displaced", used the average household size where a document counted only households, and, because the documents do not consistently separate temporary impacts from permanent ones, "decided to include all impacts", down to a loss as small as under one per cent of a person's land or income. It drew mainly on resettlement action plans, which are written before the work is done, and used completion reports where no resettlement plan existed. Its data stops at 31 December 2014. cases.title: Cuijiaying complex on the Han River: 57 households, 223 people
cases.place: Cuijiaying navigation complex, Han River below Xiangyang (Xiangfan), Hubei, China
cases.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on the Cuijiaying navigation complex on the Han River, downstream of the city of Xiangyang, formerly Xiangfan, in Hubei. The loan also paid for channel works on the Han River and for studies, so land was taken along a river reach as well as at the dam.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Fifth Inland Waterways Project, P085333. Loan IBRD-48040 of US$100 million, approved 11 October 2005, effective 13 December 2005, closed 30 June 2011 with no extension. The loan was fully disbursed at US$100 million.

cases.conditions: The loan triggered the Bank's policies on involuntary resettlement, safety of dams and cultural property. A resettlement action plan and an environmental management plan were prepared before approval. The completion report says measures to protect the environment were written into the contract documents.

companies.name: Cuijiaying Complex Management Office
companies.role: Ran the construction and later the operation of the navigation complex

cases.community: The recorded physical displacement is 223 people. The completion report says the resettlement plan was finished in September 2009. In total 37,541 mu of land, 2,503 hectares, was acquired; 57 households with 223 people were relocated; 23 business enterprises were compensated; and affected community assets were replaced. All 57 households were moved within the same village and given new cement-brick houses with modern amenities that the report says were much better than their old homes. At the dam site, the farmers who lost the most land were compensated at rates higher than the resettlement plan provided. 34 vulnerable people were given a monthly pension of RMB 100 to 300. 24 small family businesses, which employed 55 farmers, were moved to National Road 207, and each household there was able to rent out part of its house for extra income. In the reservoir area the affected villages lost less than five per cent of their land. The report says 77.5 per cent of the households interviewed by the external monitor said their life was better than before the project. The project built a dam about 18 metres high with a shiplock. No village is named in either document.
cases.outcome: The resettlement is recorded as compliant. The completion report of 19 December 2011 says compliance with the resettlement plan could be considered highly satisfactory and that the plan was carried out without rancour or dispute. The completion report rates the project outcome Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory, borrower performance Satisfactory and risk to the development outcome Low or Negligible. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 14 January 2013 disagrees on two of those: it rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory and Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory, keeping borrower performance Satisfactory and risk Negligible to Low. Its reason for the lower outcome rating is that the project's stated aim stressed raising the standard of living in the Han River region, but the causal link from the project's activities to that was weak and not backed by sufficient evidence; for the Bank rating, that monitoring specified no indicator for standard of living. The review also notes that the completion report's claim that income per head at the dam area rose from just over 3,000 yuan before the project to over 5,000 yuan in 2010 comes from the borrower's own completion report, using survey results from the resettled families, with no counterfactual and no sign of whether the figures are adjusted for inflation. Neither document records a failure in the resettlement.

On ICIJ's own account of its method, its figures count what the Bank's documents call project-affected people: ICIJ searched those documents for the words "affected", "PAP" and "displaced", used the average household size where a document counted only households, and, because the documents do not consistently separate temporary impacts from permanent ones, "decided to include all impacts", down to a loss as small as under one per cent of a person's land or income. It drew mainly on resettlement action plans, which are written before the work is done, and used completion reports where no resettlement plan existed. Its data stops at 31 December 2014. No figure matching 25,655 appears in the completion report or in the Independent Evaluation Group's review, and the documents do not say how ICIJ arrived at it.

cases.title: Naji complex on the You River: 131 households moved against 49 planned
cases.place: Naji navigation complex, You River, Tianyang, Baise, Guangxi, China, and the Xiniu complex on the Lian River, Guangdong
cases.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on the You River in Tianyang, Baise prefecture, Guangxi, at the Naji navigation complex, where the recorded relocation happened. The same loan also built the Xiniu navigation complex on the Lian River in Guangdong, about 600 km east, and dredged shoals between Baise and Nanning; the Guangdong land take is given separately below.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Fourth Inland Waterways Project, P077137. Loan IBRD-47280 of US$91 million, approved 25 March 2004, effective 9 January 2005. The closing date moved from 31 January 2010 to 30 June 2011. US$90.55 million of the US$91 million was disbursed.

cases.conditions: The loan triggered the Bank's policy on involuntary resettlement. Resettlement plans were prepared for the Guangxi and Guangdong components before approval. The completion report says a resettlement supervisor and an external monitor were engaged to watch the work in Guangxi, and that environmental monitoring reports were sent to the Bank regularly as the project agreement required.

companies.name: Guangxi Xijiang Waterway Construction and Development Company (GXWCDC)
companies.role: Implementing agency for the Guangxi component, including the Naji complex; it ran the resettlement with local governments

companies.name: Guangdong Provincial Waterway Bureau
companies.role: Implementing agency for the Guangdong component, including the Xiniu complex

cases.community: The documents set the outcome against the plan. In Guangxi, where the project built a 20 metre high dam at Naji on the You River between Baise and Nanning, total land acquisition came to 864 hectares, 4.2 per cent above the resettlement plan. 131 households with 559 persons were relocated and rehabilitated, against 49 households and 151 persons estimated in the plan, which is 82 households more than planned. 15,622 square metres of new brick and concrete homes were rebuilt, against 16,532 square metres planned. The local government raised the land compensation rate at the dam site, and with compensation in the reservoir area rising sharply, RMB 236.7 million was paid out against a budget of RMB 66.0 million. The Independent Evaluation Group records average income per head at the dam site rising 112 per cent between 2003 and 2008 and 32 per cent in the reservoir area, and that all the relocated households were able to build brick-concrete houses. In Guangdong the land take also ran over: the completion report gives one figure of 82.4 hectares against 56.6 hectares planned, about 46 per cent more, in the same paragraph where it says compensation rates were generally higher than the plan provided, and a different figure of 77.8 hectares, an increase of 50 per cent, in its list of changes in scope. The Evaluation Group prints 82.4 hectares and states that no households were relocated in the Guangdong portion. The increase in the Guangdong land take was concentrated in the villages of Zhangwu and Hetou, and the Evaluation Group says other villages went more or less according to plan. It records that at the Xiniu dam site the rise in compensation rates was as much as 36 per cent for paddy fields and about 45 per cent at Longma and Lianyao, that the overall resettlement cost in Guangdong was 31 per cent above the planned RMB 56 million, that the living standard of households affected by resettlement improved by some 23.7 per cent and income per head by 28.5 per cent, with household income from retail and services rising from 7.2 per cent to 22.5 per cent of the total, that all structures replacing affected assets were examined and found to comply with the agreements reached with affected stakeholders, and that the external monitoring concluded the standard of living of affected persons had been restored. More households moved than planned, and more land was taken than planned; those are facts about the estimates, and neither document records anyone being harmed by the overrun.
cases.outcome: The resettlement is recorded as compliant. The completion report of 28 December 2011 says that in Guangxi land acquisition and resettlement were implemented satisfactorily and without undue hardship. It rates the project outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory, borrower performance Moderately Satisfactory and risk to the development outcome Low. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 14 January 2013 also rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, and rates both Bank and borrower performance Moderately Satisfactory. The Evaluation Group gives as its reason on Bank performance an insufficient assessment of the needs and process requirements for land acquisition, and on borrower performance a lack of wider planning perspective with respect to the Naji dam and delays in the Guangdong portion. Neither document records a failure in the resettlement itself.
cases.displaced_label: persons relocated in Guangxi, in 131 households, against 151 persons in 49 households planned (World Bank completion report)
cases.displaced_note: The World Bank's completion report gives the outcome: at the Naji navigation complex in Guangxi, 131 households with 559 persons were relocated and rehabilitated against the 49 households and 151 persons estimated in the resettlement plan, and 864 hectares of land was acquired. The Independent Evaluation Group states that no households were relocated in the Guangdong part of the project, where 82.4 hectares was taken. ICIJ puts displacement for this project at 16,805 and lists it as confirmed displacement. On ICIJ's own account of its method, its figures count what the Bank's documents call project-affected people: ICIJ searched those documents for the words "affected", "PAP" and "displaced", used the average household size where a document counted only households, and, because the documents do not consistently separate temporary impacts from permanent ones, "decided to include all impacts", down to a loss as small as under one per cent of a person's land or income. It drew mainly on resettlement action plans, which are written before the work is done, and used completion reports where no resettlement plan existed. Its data stops at 31 December 2014. No figure matching 16,805 appears in either document, and the documents do not say how ICIJ arrived at it.

cases.confidence_note: The core account rests on one body of evidence. The World Bank is reporting on its own project: the completion report is written by Bank staff with a borrower section, and the Independent Evaluation Group's review is a validation of that report. Searches, including searches in Chinese, found no press report, no NGO field research, no court record and no Inspection Panel complaint about this resettlement. cases.ecosystem: The project built a 20 metre high dam at Naji on the You River in Guangxi, creating a reservoir, and a 10.5 metre high dam at Xiniu on the Lian River in Guangdong, and dredged shoals on the You River between Baise and Nanning and on the middle reaches of the Beijiang River. A fish passage was added to the Xiniu complex late in construction after the State Environmental Protection Administration refused a design change that would have left it out. 864 hectares was acquired in Guangxi and 82.4 hectares in Guangdong. The channel works on the Beijiang River had to be redesigned after the river changed course between Suoyitan and Jiangwannan. cases.title: Second Rural Energy Project, Vietnam: 178 families lose more than a tenth of their land
cases.place: Rural distribution lines and substations in 25 provinces, Vietnam; the recorded land loss is in Vinh Phuc
cases.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on Vinh Yen, the capital of Vinh Phuc province north-west of Hanoi. Vinh Phuc is the only one of the six first-phase provinces where the appraisal document's table records families losing more than a tenth of their productive land. The project itself rebuilt and extended low and medium voltage lines in about 1,200 to 1,500 communes across 25 provinces, so the land it touched is spread the length of the country.

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA)
lenders.role: Second Rural Energy Project, P074688. Credit IDA-40000 of SDR 151.1 million (US$220 million equivalent), approved 18 November 2004, effective 31 October 2005, with additional financing credit IDA-45760 of SDR 133.8 million (US$200 million) approved in 2009, trust fund TF-54464 and a Global Environment Facility grant of US$5.25 million. The completion report covers credits totalling SDR 284.9 million (US$420 million equivalent). The project was restructured on 21 May 2009 and 16 December 2013; the closing date moved from 31 December 2011 to 30 June 2014. The project was Environmental Category B.

cases.conditions: The credit triggered the Bank's policy on involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12) and its policy on indigenous peoples. A resettlement policy framework and more than twenty provincial resettlement action plans were prepared. Because Vietnamese and Bank rules on compensation differ, the appraisal document records that the project required a waiver by the Vietnamese government of articles of its own decrees and regulations on compensation and resettlement. The integrated safeguards data sheet states that land and other assets were to be compensated at substitution cost, that crop compensation would be paid in cash at current market rates, and that particular attention would be paid to making sure the amounts in government tariffs were adjusted to match those rates.

companies.name: Electricity of Vietnam (EVN)
companies.role: Implementing agency, through provincial project management units and the regional power companies

companies.name: Ministry of Industry and Trade of Vietnam

cases.community: What the Bank's documents record is land loss along power lines, mostly temporary, not a mass of people moving house. The appraisal document of 21 October 2004 sorts the impacts into seven categories, five of them temporary right-of-way impacts. Its table for the six first-phase provinces gives a total of 178 families losing more than 10 per cent of their productive land holding, all of them in Vinh Phuc, against 299,746 square metres of land acquired permanently and 14,256,140 square metres acquired temporarily; the table carries a note that the numbers could differ from the detailed measurement survey carried out later. The safeguards data sheet of 24 May 2004 states that "the Project will not involve any major resettlement but will entail land acquisition and resettlement impacts due to construction of new lines and substations", that "in the first phase of project 131,955 households will be affected by the Project" and that the number is high "because of the DPs are scattered along the lines", that "most of impacts on land will be temporary", and that "impacts on houses will be mostly partial and generally will not require the relocation of families outside their residential plots". The completion report of 13 December 2014 says the negative impacts were generally minor because most lines were rebuilt on existing routes and only a small volume of land was acquired for new alignments and substations. It lists four difficulties met during the work: lack of cooperation of local authorities in some provinces, illegal encroachment by local people into pre-defined rights of way, long negotiations between investors and affected households over compensation packages, and initial lack of cooperation from affected communities. It also says land acquisition went more smoothly where provincial project units ran it than where the power companies did, because the provinces could direct district and commune authorities while the power companies had to work through a district compensation council.
cases.outcome: The land acquisition is recorded as compliant. The completion report says that at the end of the project overall compliance with the social safeguard policies triggered was Satisfactory, and that independent monitoring consultants were hired to assess the resettlement plans and the ethnic minorities development plan. The completion report rates the project outcome Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory, borrower performance Satisfactory and risk to the development outcome Moderate. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 12 May 2015 gives the same four ratings and records no disagreement. Neither document gives any figure for people physically moved, and neither records a failure.
cases.displaced_label: families losing more than 10 per cent of their productive land holding, in the six first-phase provinces (World Bank appraisal document)
cases.displaced_note: The World Bank's own documents do not give a count of people moved out of their homes by this project. The appraisal document's table for the six first-phase provinces gives 178 families losing more than 10 per cent of their productive land holding, all in Vinh Phuc, with 299,746 square metres of land acquired permanently and 14,256,140 square metres temporarily. The safeguards data sheet says 131,955 households would be affected in the first phase, that most land impacts would be temporary, and that impacts on houses would be mostly partial and generally would not require families to move off their residential plots. ICIJ puts displacement for this project at 773,838 and lists it as confirmed displacement. On ICIJ's own account of its method, its figures count what the Bank's documents call project-affected people: ICIJ searched those documents for the words "affected", "PAP" and "displaced", used the average household size where a document counted only households, and, because the documents do not consistently separate temporary impacts from permanent ones, "decided to include all impacts", down to a loss as small as under one per cent of a person's land or income. It drew mainly on resettlement action plans, which are written before the work is done, and used completion reports where no resettlement plan existed. Its data stops at 31 December 2014. ICIJ marks its figure for this project with a footnote, which on its method page means a project that affected more than 20,000 people but where Bank documents said most were expected to experience only minor impacts. The figure 773,838 appears in none of the five core project documents, and the documents do not say how ICIJ arrived at it. The project's file holds 91 items, including more than twenty provincial resettlement action plans, which were not all read, so this is a statement about the five core documents and not about the whole file.

cases.title: Vietnam Water Resources Assistance: 5,974 households affected, 65 required resettlement
cases.place: Six irrigation schemes - Phu Ninh (Quang Nam), Yen Lap (Quang Ninh), Dau Tieng (Tay Ninh and Ho Chi Minh City), Cau Son-Cam Son, Ke Go and Da Ban - Vietnam
cases.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on Tam Ky, the capital of Quang Nam province, which holds the Phu Ninh irrigation scheme and the Vu Gia-Thu Bon river basin the project drew up a plan for. The project rehabilitated six separate irrigation schemes in different parts of the country, named in the place field, so no single point covers the land that was taken.

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA)
lenders.role: Water Resources Assistance Project, P065898. Credit IDA-38800 (Credit No. C3880) of SDR 105.7 million (US$157.8 million equivalent), with trust fund TF-54751, approved 30 March 2004, effective 21 December 2004. The closing date moved from 31 December 2011 to 31 December 2012 in a one-year no-cost extension. Total project cost at completion was SDR 102.83 million (US$159.44 million equivalent).

cases.conditions: The credit was Environmental Category A and triggered seven Bank safeguard policies: environmental assessment, natural habitats, pest management, cultural property, involuntary resettlement, indigenous peoples and safety of dams. A resettlement framework and seven detailed resettlement plans were prepared for the six schemes. An ethnic minority development plan was required where minority households were affected.

companies.name: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development of Vietnam
companies.role: Borrower's implementing ministry; provincial project implementation offices led the work

cases.community: The figures here come from a field-based evaluation. The Independent Evaluation Group's Project Performance Assessment Report of 20 August 2019, written after a mission that visited Vietnam in March 2019 and three of the six irrigation schemes, states: "In all, 5,974 households were negatively affected; of these 167 households were classified as 'severely affected' with loses of more than 20 percent of their land. Sixty-five households required resettlement." It records that ethnic minorities were affected in one of the six schemes, Cau Son-Cam Son, where 69 households of the Tay and Nung minorities were affected, and that the provincial project management unit prepared and carried out an ethnic minority development plan to compensate them. It says the project caused temporary or permanent loss of the use of some land and property because of the construction and the new infrastructure. It also records that gender and poverty aspects were not specifically monitored by the social surveys or by the project's monitoring system, which it calls a missed opportunity to assess project benefits in those areas.
cases.outcome: The resettlement is recorded as compliant. The 2019 assessment says overall environmental and social safeguards compliance was adequate, based on the implementation status reports, the completion report and the final report on carrying out the resettlement action plans. The assessment prints three ratings side by side and they agree: the completion report, the Independent Evaluation Group's earlier review and the 2019 assessment all rate the project outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory, borrower performance Moderately Satisfactory and risk to the development outcome Moderate. The Evaluation Group's review of 9 December 2013 records that a social safeguards assessment and a review of the technical design of the works "was able to reduce the number of affected households from the initial 11,000 to about 6,000, although the ICR does not evaluate the adequacy of the compensation package". That is an absence of evaluation, not a finding that compensation was inadequate. The 2013 review also records that the environmental management plan was not effectively monitored at the start and that the appointment of an environmental monitoring consultant was delayed by three years, after which monitoring improved considerably.
cases.displaced_label: households that required resettlement, out of 5,974 negatively affected and 167 classified as severely affected (Independent Evaluation Group field assessment, 2019)
cases.displaced_note: The Independent Evaluation Group's field-based assessment of 2019 gives 5,974 households negatively affected, of which 167 were classified as severely affected with losses of more than 20 per cent of their land, and 65 households that required resettlement. ICIJ puts displacement for this project at 53,600 and lists it as confirmed displacement. On ICIJ's own account of its method, its figures count what the Bank's documents call project-affected people: ICIJ searched those documents for the words "affected", "PAP" and "displaced", used the average household size where a document counted only households, and, because the documents do not consistently separate temporary impacts from permanent ones, "decided to include all impacts", down to a loss as small as under one per cent of a person's land or income. It drew mainly on resettlement action plans, which are written before the work is done, and used completion reports where no resettlement plan existed. Its data stops at 31 December 2014. ICIJ marks its figure for this project with a footnote, which on its method page means a project that affected more than 20,000 people but where Bank documents said most were expected to experience only minor impacts. ICIJ's 53,600 is of the same order as the project's initial estimate of 11,000 affected households, which the Evaluation Group's 2013 review says a safeguards assessment and design review cut to about 6,000. The documents do not say how ICIJ arrived at its figure.

cases.title: Vietnam Distribution Efficiency Project: five households relocated out of 12,880 affected
cases.place: Electricity distribution subprojects in 27 provinces, Vietnam, including Ha Noi and Dong Nai
cases.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on Hanoi, one of the two places the completion report names where land acquisition was difficult, the other being Dong Nai province. The project built or rebuilt 169 electricity distribution subprojects across 27 provinces through five power corporations, so the land it touched is spread the length of the country.

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA)
lenders.role: Distribution Efficiency Project, P125996. Credit IDA-51560 of SDR 297.7 million (US$448.9 million equivalent), with trust funds TF-13456 and TF-13468, approved 11 September 2012, effective 7 February 2013, restructured 22 June 2016, closed 31 December 2018 on its original closing date. A grant from AusAID of US$8 million was reduced to US$6.2 million at effectiveness.

cases.conditions: The credit triggered the Bank's policy on involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12) and its policy on indigenous peoples (OP 4.10). A resettlement policy framework, an ethnic minority policy framework and, where relevant, resettlement action plans and ethnic minority development plans were prepared, cleared and published. The frameworks and the environmental management plans were disclosed in Vietnamese at the Vietnam Development Information Center, at Electricity of Vietnam, at the project management units and in the subproject provinces, and in English at the Bank's Infoshop.

companies.name: Northern, Central, Southern, Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City Power Corporations
companies.role: The five power corporations that built the 169 subprojects and ran the land acquisition and compensation

cases.community: The scale of this project's physical displacement is five households. The completion report of 14 June 2019 states: "The PCs were able to minimize physical relocation (only five households were relocated out of 12,880 Project Affected Households) by the construction/execution of 169 subprojects", and adds that "although the number of affected households was high (owing to the inherent nature of linear projects), the impact at household level was low and/manageable". Compensation paid to affected households totalled VND 287 billion, about US$12.4 million. As of 31 May 2019 the social safeguard instruments had been completed in 167 of the 169 subprojects, 98.8 per cent, with two outstanding, one for the Hanoi Power Corporation and one for the Southern Power Corporation, where civil works and land acquisition had started and were due to finish by 30 June 2019. The report says consultation with affected households, local communities and local authorities was carried out as the two safeguard policies require, and that the power corporations carried out all the proposed mitigation measures. It also says that, in hindsight, the project could have benefited from more advance consultation on the ground with local communities in areas prone to more difficult land acquisition. The completion report names Ha Noi and Dong Nai as places where land acquisition was difficult; the Evaluation Group records that delayed approvals for land acquisition meant the works portion of five subprojects could not be finished within the project's life, so the project financed only the materials for them.
cases.outcome: The resettlement is recorded as compliant. The completion report says the safeguards rating at project close was Satisfactory for both environmental and social safeguards and that the project complied with all the safeguard policies triggered throughout its life. The completion report rates the project outcome Highly Satisfactory, Bank performance Highly Satisfactory and the quality of monitoring High. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 21 January 2020 gives the same three ratings and records no disagreement. Neither document records a failure in the land acquisition. Both record a lesson drawn from it: that involving local authorities early is critical to safeguard work, and that land acquisition and resettlement for investments are becoming increasingly difficult in Vietnam.

On ICIJ's own account of its method, its figures count what the Bank's documents call project-affected people: ICIJ searched those documents for the words "affected", "PAP" and "displaced", used the average household size where a document counted only households, and, because the documents do not consistently separate temporary impacts from permanent ones, "decided to include all impacts", down to a loss as small as under one per cent of a person's land or income. It drew mainly on resettlement action plans, which are written before the work is done, and used completion reports where no resettlement plan existed. Its data stops at 31 December 2014. ICIJ marks its figure for this project with a footnote, which on its method page means a project that affected more than 20,000 people but where Bank documents said most were expected to experience only minor impacts. The completion report's five households are a count of physical relocation; ICIJ's 31,581 is a count of project-affected people. The documents do not say how ICIJ arrived at its figure.

cases.title: National Highways Interconnectivity, India: 11,138 people affected across eleven corridors
cases.place: Eleven national highway corridors in Bihar, Rajasthan, Odisha, Karnataka and West Bengal, India
cases.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on Patna, the capital of Bihar, the state with the largest share of the works: 499 km of the 1,120 km originally planned, and the four roads where the Independent Evaluation Group says land acquisition needs were inaccurately identified. The project ran along eleven road corridors in five states, so no single point covers the land that was taken. Neither Bank document names the eleven corridors by highway number.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: National Highways Interconnectivity Improvement Project, P121185. Loan IBRD-83010 of US$500 million, approved 29 October 2013, effective 5 August 2014, mid-term review 12 May 2017. The closing date moved from 30 June 2019 to 30 September 2020. The road component was costed at US$1,106.4 million including US$468.05 million of Bank money, and came in at US$704.0 million including US$293.6 million of Bank money.

cases.conditions: The loan triggered the Bank's policy on involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12) and its policy on indigenous peoples (OP 4.10), the latter because six of the corridors, in Odisha, Rajasthan and West Bengal, ran through areas where indigenous communities live. Corridor-specific resettlement action plans were prepared under a resettlement policy framework and published in India and at the Bank's InfoShop. Indigenous peoples development plans were written and their actions folded into the resettlement plans. The project required contractors to be handed 80 per cent of the land free of encumbrance within a set period, and gave grievance redressal committees a role in deciding eligibility where the plan's figures and what was found on the ground differed.

companies.name: National Highways Authority of India / Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
companies.role: Borrower's implementing bodies; state public works departments carried out the land acquisition

cases.community: The completion report of 29 June 2022 gives the scale: "The project impacted 775 acres of land, including 558 acres of private land, 6390 structures (including 451 CPRs) and 11,138 PAPs", CPRs being common property resources and PAPs project-affected people. It says that at closure "compensation and eligible assistance were duly paid to all PAPs in six of the 11 road corridors", and that the remaining five roads, in Bihar and West Bengal, were transferred to another Bank-funded project, the Green National Highway Corridors Project, where the outstanding resettlement actions would be monitored. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 21 February 2023 records that "disbursement of compensation to project-affected people (PAPs) were substantially delayed in several sections but by project closing, all 11,138 PAPs were compensated for land acquisition for the subprojects completed under the project". The two statements describe the same set of completed corridors, so what the record holds is a delay with no length, no date and no number of people attached to it. Both documents record that the land acquisition was mis-sized: the completion report says poor road designs led to inaccurate assessments of land acquisition needs, and the Evaluation Group says needs were inaccurately identified for four roads in Bihar because of inadequate road designs, which led to variations in the number of project-affected people, and that road designs were revised to avoid bypasses that needed land acquisition. The project received 347 grievances and the completion report says all but one were resolved. No village or neighbourhood is named in either document.
cases.outcome: The resettlement is recorded as substantially done, with a delay that neither document quantifies. The completion report rates the project outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory and the quality of monitoring Modest. The Independent Evaluation Group's review gives the same three ratings and records no disagreement; it rates the quality of the completion report itself Modest. At closing 704 km of the 856 km planned in the three low-income states had been built, 82 per cent, and 212 km of the 215 km planned in the two middle-income states, 99 per cent; 155 km of civil works was unfinished and was moved to the Green National Highway Corridors Project, where 102 km of it had been completed by 31 March 2022.

On ICIJ's own account of its method, its figures count what the Bank's documents call project-affected people: ICIJ searched those documents for the words "affected", "PAP" and "displaced", used the average household size where a document counted only households, and, because the documents do not consistently separate temporary impacts from permanent ones, "decided to include all impacts", down to a loss as small as under one per cent of a person's land or income. It drew mainly on resettlement action plans, which are written before the work is done, and used completion reports where no resettlement plan existed. Its data stops at 31 December 2014. No figure matching 23,016 appears in the completion report or in the Independent Evaluation Group's review, and the documents do not say how ICIJ arrived at it.

cases.ecosystem: The completion report records that the design of subprojects was changed where forest land had to be diverted or where wildlife corridors were crossed. 775 acres of land was taken, 558 acres of it private, and 6,390 structures were affected, including 451 common property resources such as handpumps, some of which were relocated in consultation with communities and in coordination with the Integrated Tribal Development Agency.

lvwhy.project: A World Bank loan of US$500 million part-financed the widening of the eleven highway corridors that took the land.
lvwhy.land: 775 acres was taken for road widening and bypasses under corridor-specific resettlement action plans attached to the loan.
